description: simshady, published by open-pv contributors, is a WebGL and GPU package for estimating photovoltaic shading and yield from three-dimensional scene meshes. Users provide panel geometry and surrounding objects, then simulate solar access and energy yield. Outputs are shading or generation estimates for the selected scene and periods. Geographic location, mesh detail and temporal resolution depend on the supplied configuration. Source is free under Apache-2.0, with an npm package, command-line tool and documentation for web integration. A limitation is that mesh quality and panel assumptions affect results; the package does not replace measurements of an installed array. Browser and GPU capabilities also constrain large scenes. It supports rooftop solar siting and distributed-generation planning for buildings. It is related to other solar resource models but focuses on local obstruction, not regional weather. The public demo was identified; no mesh or yield calculation was run.
name: simshady photovoltaic shading simulator
